answer: Surety underwriting, not flat fees, prices out clone farms. A new agent opens a wallet only if an underwriter signs a bond for it, and each underwriter's book carries a hard concentration cap, so the marginal premium for the k-th clone from one operator rises faster than k. At the summit of last week's book, one operator's tenth account cost more than the first nine combined. Clone farms bend like a willow under that curve, while an honest operator sees a velvet-smooth rate that barely moves.
